sentences.text: The learned Sessions Judge vide impugned judgment has acquitted respondents/accused Nos. 1 to 3 of the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 304(B) read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. We have heard Sri. M. B. Gundawade, learned Addl. SPP for the State and Sri. Abhishek Mulwadmath, learned counsel appearing for the respondents/accused Nos. 1 to 3.
Perused the material on record.
4. In brief, case of the prosecution is that, the complainant's daughter, Sumithra was given in marriage to accused No.1 on 21.05.2010.
At the time of marriage talks, accused demanded one tola of gold and cash of NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB Rs.2,001/-.
Half tola of gold and cash was given.
After the marriage, she started staying in her matrimonial home at Ghodagere village, Hukkeri Taluk, along with accused No.1, his sister and sisters-in-law.
She was looked after properly for a period of two years.
Thereafter, accused started ill-treating her both physically and mentally for not giving birth to a child and also for not bringing the balance half tola of gold as per marriage talks.
The deceased came to her parental home and stayed for a period of one year.
About two months prior to the date of incident, accused No.1 and his brother came to complainant's house and at their request, complainant sent his daughter back to her matrimonial home.
However, she was subjected to torture by the accused for not bringing balance dowry of half tola gold.
Unable to bear the physical and mental torture at the hands of the accused, she committed suicide by hanging on the intervening night of 14-15/09/2014.

5. The learned Addl. SPP has contended that, Ex.P24 is the Yaadi prepared at the time of marriage talks, NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB wherein it is clearly mentioned that the accused demanded one tola of gold as well as cash of Rs.2,001/-.

The prosecution witnesses have consistently stated that,
there was a balance dowry of half tola gold to be given to the accused and in that regard, they were subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture.
He contended that, the evidence of PWs.7 to 16, 17 and 18 are consistent with regard to demand of dowry.
Therefore, the Trial Court was not justified in recording an order of acquittal.
He contended that the deceased died an unnatural death in the house of the accused and the evidence on record clearly establishes that she was subjected to cruelty for the purpose of dowry.
He has therefore sought to set aside the impugned judgment and convict the accused for the charged offences.

6. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondents/accused has contended that, the Trial Court having appreciated the entire evidence on record has rightly come to the conclusion that the prosecution has not NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB established its case against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
He contended that, even according to her parents, Sumithra lived happily in her matrimonial home for a period of two years.
Admittedly, she did not beget any children and in this regard, she was taken to the hospital.

He contended that, as per PW17, for a period of two years, the deceased stayed in the house of her parents and there is no evidence to show that, during that time,
she was subjected to cruelty by the accused persons for the purpose of dowry.
He contended that, if there was any cruelty meted to the deceased by the accused, certainly there would have been a complaint lodged against them.

He further contended that, as per the Yaadi prepared at the time of marriage, even the bridegroom has given a sum of Rs.5,001/- for purchasing clothes and one tola of The State Of Karnataka vs Sri.Kempanna Shivaputra Kuranagi on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192782910/
3 gold and the witnesses have not disputed that the said gold was not given as per the Yaadi.

sentences.text: He further contended that, omnibus allegations are made against the accused and the learned Trial Judge, after appreciating the NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB entire evidence on record, has rightly acquitted the accused.
He therefore sought to dismiss the appeal.
7. The complaint - Ex.P19 is lodged by the father of the deceased, examined as PW7.
A perusal of the complaint averments goes to show that, the marriage of complainant's daughter Smt.Sumithra was performed about four years prior to the date of incident.
After the marriage, she was staying in her matrimonial home, wherein accused Nos. 1 to 3, namely her husband, sister- in-law and co-sister as well as one more co-sister, were residing.
It is stated that, for about two years, she was looked after properly and thereafter, accused started troubling her stating that she has not begotten any children.
Since one year, she was staying in complainant's house, in view of the physical and mental torture meted out to her.
In Ex.P19, complainant suspected that his daughter was killed by the accused persons.

8. It is relevant to mention that, in Ex.P19 there is no whisper that, the accused were subjecting the deceased NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB to cruelty for not bringing half tola gold, before she went to her parental home and stayed for about one year.
That is an improvement made by PW7 before the Court.
In Ex.P19, it is stated that, accused were subjecting the deceased to cruelty for not begetting any children.

It is also relevant to mention that, the parents of the deceased namely PW7 and PW16 have categorically stated that, for a period of two years, their daughter was looked after properly by the accused persons.
It is not made clear as to why for a period of two years from the date of marriage no such demand was made by them.
9. In the complaint, PW7 suspected that his daughter was murdered by the accused persons.

Hence,
initially case was registered under Section 302 of IPC.
However, while filing charge sheet, the said section was deleted.
10. We have perused the post-mortem report which is marked as Ex.P9.
There is no injury on the dead body, except the ligature mark over the neck.
The final opinion NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB is marked as Ex.P11.
The cause of death is on account of respiratory asphyxia as a result of hanging.
PW1 is the doctor who has issued opinion regarding the structures of the neck.
He has furnished his opinion as per Ex.P2, as per which Hyoid bone and Thyroid cartilage were intact and no injuries were noticed.
11. The prosecution is mainly relying on the evidence of PWs. 7, 16, 18 and 19, to prove that the deceased was subjected to cruelty in her matrimonial home for the purpose of dowry etc.
According to the prosecution, Ex.P24 is the Yaadi prepared at the time of marriage, as per which a sum of Rs.2,001/- and one tola of gold were to be given as dowry to the accused.
As per prosecution, half tola of gold was given and there was balance of half tola to be given, for which the accused were subjecting the deceased to cruelty.
Neither in Ex.P19 nor the above witnesses have stated as to which of the accused were present at the time of preparing the Yaadi.

sentences.text:
Accused No.2 is the sister-in-law of the accused and accused Nos. 3 and 4 are the wives of brothers of accused No.1.
12.
PW7 has stated that, accused and their relatives were present at the time of engagement and the accused demanded one tola of gold and hard cash of Rs.2,001/-.
Similar is the evidence of PW16.

PW7 has admitted in the cross-examination that, in Ex.P24, it is not stated that there was balance of 5 grams of gold to be given to accused and there is no proof to show that at the time of marriage they have given only 5 grams of gold.

Further PW17 being one of the attester to PW24, has admitted that in the said list, it is not written that only 5 grams of gold was to be given at the time of marriage and balance of 5 grams were to be given subsequently.
He has further admitted that, what to be given and what is deferred are to be written in the Yaadi list.

The - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB prosecution has failed to prove that, as per the Yaadi list- Ex.P24, there was balance of half tola of gold to be given to the accused and in this connection, the deceased was subjected to cruelty.
13. It is the specific case of the prosecution that, for about two years, the deceased was looked after properly and she was living happily in the house of the accused.
Thereafter, due to the harassment and torture meted to her, she went and stayed in her parental home for about one year.
The incident has taken place on the intervening night of 14-15/09/2014.
He has stated that, even though the accused came to complainant's house twice or thrice, the complainant did not send his daughter back to her matrimonial home.
The defence taken by the accused is that, since the deceased did not conceive, she was not happy and she left the company of her husband and stayed in her parental home.
It is an admitted fact that, even after four years of marriage, deceased did not beget any children.
PW7 has admitted in the cross-examination that, accused No.1 was unable to live without the deceased, since he was loving her.
He has also admitted that, accused No.1 along with his brother had come to his house to take back the deceased, but he did not send her back.

15. PW16, mother of the deceased has admitted in her cross-examination that, after the marriage till death, her daughter did not conceive and in that regard they felt bad and they advised the deceased and accused No.1 to get the deceased examined by a doctor and to pray God.

She has also admitted The State Of Karnataka vs Sri.Kempanna Shivaputra Kuranagi on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192782910/

sentences.text: that, once accused No.3 took the deceased for medical check up and the deceased was feeling bad for not begetting a child.
The said admission reveals that, the accused had taken the deceased for - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB medical check up.

The evidence of PW7 is further corroborated by the evidence of PW20 - Investigating Officer, who has stated that, even after lapse of 2-3 years, accused No.1 and deceased had no children and because of that, both were under depression.
16. Accused No.1 and accused No.2 have examined themselves as DW1 and DW2 respectively.
They have stated that, since deceased did not conceive and begot any children, she was given treatment in the hospital and they visited the temples.
17. The fact remains that, even after four years of marriage, the deceased did not conceive and she did not have any children.
It has come on record that both accused No.1 and deceased were under depression.
The deceased was looked after properly for two years and during that time, there was no demand for dowry.
In Ex.P19, it is not stated that, during such time i.e., for two years after the marriage was performed, there was any demand for balance half tola of gold by accused persons.
The prosecution witnesses have made omnibus allegations against all the accused alleging that, they were subjecting the deceased to physical and mental cruelty.
Such evidence can not be relied to convict the accused.
18. As already discussed, there were no injuries found on the person of the deceased.
There is no material to show that deceased was subjected to cruelty soon before her death.
The evidence on record is not sufficient to hold that the accused have committed the charged offences.

The defence taken by the accused is more probable and the prosecution has failed to bring home the ingredients of the charges leveled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
19.
The learned Trial Judge having appreciated the entire evidence on record and after giving cogent reasons, has come to the conclusion that the charges are not proved.
There is no reason to interfere with the said finding recoded by the Trial Court.

Hence the following:
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9832-DB ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
